In this three-step algorithm, we gradually increase the level of complexity of the optimization problems to improve convergence and robustness of the method. For instance, the optimization problem of Step 1 is easier to solve compared to the other steps since it has fewer design variables and constraints. The Step 2 optimization problem is more complex, however we start with a feasible design which is the optimal design of Step 1, so we expect well-behaved convergence. The most difficult problem to solve is that of Step 3, however the initial design is close to feasible and close to optimal since we use the solution of the Step 2. We explored other solution strategies to solve the optimization problem, but none of them worked as well as the three-step method.
